extraInstructions: IMPORTANT: Do NOT use speechManager.speak() anywhere in the game. Only use audioManager.play() for sound effects. Valid sound effects: pickup, drop-correct, drop-wrong, tap, success, error, celebration, hint. The game must teach: (1) Numbers up to 99 — read and write numbers up to 99, number names (one, two...ninety-nine), understand tens and ones (e.g., 45 = 4 tens and 5 ones). (2) 3-digit numbers up to 999 — read and write numbers from 100 to 999, number names (one hundred, one hundred one...nine hundred ninety-nine), understand hundreds, tens, and ones (e.g., 345 = 3 hundreds, 4 tens, 5 ones). (3) Place and face values — face value is the digit itself (in 345, face value of 4 is 4), place value is face value x position (in 345, place value of 4 is 40 because it is in the tens place). Hundreds place = x100, Tens place = x10, Ones place = x1. (4) Comparison and ordering — compare two numbers (the one with more hundreds is bigger; if hundreds are same, compare tens; if tens are same, compare ones). Ascending order = smallest to biggest. Descending order = biggest to smallest. Use > (greater than) and < (less than) symbols. Misconceptions: 'place value and face value are the same' (place value depends on position, face value is just the digit), 'in 506, the 0 means nothing' (0 in the tens place means zero tens, it is important to keep the place), 'bigger number always has more digits visible' (compare place by place, not by looking at digits randomly), '100 is the same as 1' (100 means one hundred, 1 means one — place matters). Default width=720, height=560. Use named export (export function NumbersGame), NOT export default. Export interface NumbersGameProps with width?, height?, onComplete?: (score: number) => void.
